name: UWF World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Vacant at the September 2006 restart, filled by an eight-man tournament Abyss won over Kurt Angle with outside interference from owner Matthew Hopkins and Chyna-Doll. The belt changed hands six more times on the surviving ledger — through Kurt Angle, Brock Lesnar, Sting, Christian Cage (in an elimination chamber over Sting, U.S. Champion Hulk Hogan, Paul Wight, Bill Goldberg and Ric Flair), Kurt Angle again and Ric Flair — before Matthew Hopkins stripped Flair over a real-world dispute involving Vince McMahon and the Stamford Outsiders; the tournament called to fill the vacancy never finished after a riot closed the arena. Randy Orton won the last-recorded reign in a Triple Threat against John Bradshaw Layfield and Flair.

name: UWF World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Held by the British Bulldogs at the September 2006 restart, then by the Road Warriors, AJ Styles & Christopher Daniels, Owen Hart & Jeff Jarrett (twice), Arn Anderson & Tully Blanchard, and finally Ted DiBiase Jr & Cody Rhodes on the surviving ledger.

name: UWF United States Championship
epitaph: Held by Vader at the September 2006 restart, then Sid Vicious, Hulk Hogan, Randy Savage, Roddy Piper, James Storm, Jamie Noble and Harley Race on the surviving ledger.

name: UWF Cruiserweight Championship
epitaph: Held by "American Dragon" Bryan Danielson at the September 2006 restart, then Yoshihiro Tajiri and Dean Malenko, before AJ Styles won a Cruiserweight Gauntlet Battle Royal, pinning Billy Kidman in the finale, on the surviving ledger.

name: UWF World Women's Championship
epitaph: Vacant at the September 2006 restart, filled when Sherri Martel defeated the Fabulous Moolah in a tournament final. Trish Stratus, Sherri Martel again, Bull Nakano, Sherri Martel again and finally Beth Phoenix held it on the surviving ledger.

name: UWF World Women's Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Held by the Fabulous Moolah & Mae Young at the September 2006 restart, then Lisa Morretti & Nora Greenwald, Rhonda Singh & Luna Vachon, Trish Stratus & Gail Kim (twice, with Lisa Morretti & Nora Greenwald between), and Awesome Kong & Aja Kong — the last representing ICWC in an interpromotional match — on the surviving ledger.

name: UWF World Midget Championship
epitaph: The UWF crowned its first and, on the surviving ledger, only World Midget Champion at the 2007 Ultimate Supercard: Little Beaver, in a four-way dance over Sky Low Low, the Haiti Kid and Lord Littlebrook.

name: UWF Intercontinental Championship (discontinued)
epitaph: Held by Kurt Angle at the September 2006 restart, vacated when Angle pursued the World title, then won by Scott Steiner over Raven in a tournament final. Ultimate Warrior took the belt from Steiner at Fallout 2007 and, per the fed's own ledger, carried it with him to ICWC when he moved federations — continuing as the ICWC Intercontinental Championship.

name: UWF Canadian Heavyweight Championship (discontinued)
epitaph: Held by Bad News Allen Coage at the September 2006 restart, then Bobby Rude, Sean Morley, Bad News Allen again, and finally Lance Storm. The fed's own ledger says Lance Storm carried the belt with him to XWF, but no XWF title on the surviving record continues this specific lineage — an unresolved gap.

name: UWF Television Championship (discontinued)
epitaph: Held by Ravishing Rick Rude at the September 2006 restart, then Macho Man Randy Savage and Curt Hennig, before Rick Rude reclaimed it and carried it to XWF, where Paul Heyman renamed it the North American Heavyweight Championship.

name: UWF United States Tag Team Championship (discontinued)
epitaph: Named for Demolition at the September 2006 restart. Per both feds' own ledgers, Demolition carried the title with them to XWF, where it continued as the XWF World Tag Team Championship.
